subsystem: Dashboard shell, security, install/launchers, ops, testing and CI
summary: The dashboard server, its token login, origin checks, the fail-closed bind and the resident/platform launchers are carefully built and heavily unit-tested on Linux. But the two launchers the owner actually uses have never succeeded on his laptop since the UTF-8 fix. The real Windows CI job has been failing for weeks and currently dies part-way through, so Windows coverage is worse than it looks. The repo also contains a committed copy of a real-looking dashboard token and VAPID private key, and with no token set every owner page (Home, Setup, Settings) is locked while the API is open to DNS rebinding. The older install-apex.bat, start-apex.bat and stop-apex.bat are stale and point at the wrong Python.

features.what: One console that starts Apex in resident mode with Celine's fast voice, the offline Apocalypse dashboard, and NOMAD (only if Docker Desktop is running and its images are already cached). If one service fails, the other keeps running; Ctrl+C stops what it started.

features.name: Cross-site request protection (origin check)
features.what: Every POST/PUT/DELETE must come from the dashboard's own origin (or a browser extension with a valid bearer token), so a random website cannot make Apex do things.

gaps.issue: With no DASHBOARD_TOKEN, the dashboard is open to DNS rebinding. The origin check compares Origin with the request's own Host header and there is no Host allow-list, so a malicious web page that rebinds its domain to 127.0.0.1 passes as same-origin and can POST (e.g. /api/chat to an agent with shell access) and read GET APIs (memories, tasks).
gaps.evidence: dashboard/companion.py:201-216; dashboard/server.py:232-245,262-263 (tokenless dispatch); no TrustedHostMiddleware anywhere in dashboard/
gaps.fix_hint: Reject requests whose Host is not 127.0.0.1/localhost/[::1]/the configured PUBLIC_BASE_URL or Tailscale name (TrustedHostMiddleware), or require DASHBOARD_TOKEN always.
gaps.how_confirmed: Ran a TestClient snippet with DASHBOARD_TOKEN='' and base_url http://evil.example:7860: POST /api/companion/cancel/abc with Origin http://evil.example:7860 returned 200, while Origin http://other.example returned 403. grep found no TrustedHost or Host check.

gaps.evidence: config.py:133; dashboard/server.py:262-263, 2240-2256; dashboard/home.py:14-18; scripts/run_apex_platform.py:216 opens /home; dashboard/static/setup.js:48
gaps.fix_hint: Have Apex.bat or the first start generate a random DASHBOARD_TOKEN into .env and print it once, or treat a loopback-only tokenless request as master when bound to 127.0.0.1 (after fixing the Host check above).

Check whether a login Run entry exists (reg query HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run /v Apex); if it does, Apex may already be running when you double-click the platform launcher.
Open Docker Desktop before Start-Apex-Platform.cmd if you want NOMAD and Kolibri courses.

rating.why: Careful, well-tested server and launcher code. But a leaked master token, red Windows CI that stops mid-suite, owner pages locked by default and stale install scripts mean it is not yet trustworthy on the one laptop that matters.
